passage:
Dear Rajni Masi,

You asked why I have gone quiet on the phone. The truth is that some kids in my class call me weird, poor, and other things about my body. They do it when the teacher isn't looking, and sometimes they copy how I talk. Last week someone stuck a note on my bag. I cried in the washroom and hated myself for a while. But I have been thinking: nothing they say is my fault. Their words are about them. I've started spending lunch in the art room, where nobody cares what I wear. Yesterday I showed the note to my class teacher, and she said she would deal with it. I wanted you to know, so that I'm not alone in this.

Love,
Jasleen

qa.q: Where has Jasleen started spending lunch?
How did Jasleen feel at first, and how has Jasleen's thinking changed?
qa.a: Jasleen first felt hurt and ashamed, crying in the washroom, but now believes the mocking is not Jasleen's fault and that the bullies' words are about them.

qa.q: What did Jasleen do that helps in this situation?
qa.a: Jasleen protected their self-respect by not believing the bullies' story, found a place to fit in at the art room, and reported the harassment by showing the note to the class teacher.

qa.q: How might Rajni Masi feel on reading the letter?
qa.a: Probably sad and protective, but also proud that Jasleen spoke up. She asked why Jasleen had gone quiet, so she cares and will be glad to know.

grounding: The protagonist is mocked, refuses to believe the story, finds a place to fit in and reports the harassment.

passage:
On the morning of the maths exam, the sole of Yusuf's shoe finally came off. He taped it with electrical tape and walked to school.
At the gate, a group of boys from 9C started. "Look, the beggar's new fashion!" One of them filmed his feet. The laughter followed him to the exam hall. It had been going on for months: poor boy, charity case.
Yusuf's hands shook as he sat down. For a second he believed them. Then he looked at the paper and thought, I'm better at this than all of them. That's mine.
He finished the exam. Afterwards his friend Ganga said, "That video's in the section group. We're telling Mrs Reddy. Right now."
They went together. Mrs Reddy watched the clip and said, "This is harassment, Yusuf, and it's not your fault. None of it." She had the video taken down that afternoon and called the boys' parents.
Walking home, Ganga said, "Chess club tomorrow?" Yusuf nodded. There, nobody cared about shoes.

qa.q: What did Yusuf use to fix his shoe?
How did Yusuf feel when the boys laughed at him?
qa.a: He felt humiliated and shaky, and for a moment he believed their mocking story about him.

qa.q: Which steps helped Yusuf protect his self-respect?
qa.a: He focused on his exam, reported the harassment with Ganga the same day, and kept going to the chess club where he fits in.

qa.q: How does Mrs Reddy see the boys' behaviour?
qa.a: She sees it as harassment, tells Yusuf it isn't his fault, and acts that afternoon.

grounding: A teen mocked as poor protects his self-respect, finds a space where he fits, and reports the harassment to a teacher.

passage:
In Akash's Jaipur school, some boys had a name for him: "Motu." They puffed out their cheeks when he passed and made the benches creak on purpose when he sat down.
For weeks he laughed along, to seem cool. At home he stopped eating in front of anyone and stayed in his room.
One afternoon he found a note in his bag with a cruel drawing. His friend Simran saw his face. "Enough," she said. "We're going to the counsellor."
He didn't want to. But she walked with him.
The counsellor, Ms Ahuja, looked at the drawing and said firmly, "This is harassment. It says something about them, not about you." She called Akash's parents that afternoon and spoke to the boys' class teacher.
That week, Simran dragged him to drama club auditions. He got the part of the loud, funny king. At rehearsal, people laughed with him, not at him. That felt completely different.

qa.q: Where did Akash find the cruel note?
How had Akash been feeling during the weeks of mocking?
qa.a: He felt hurt and ashamed, hiding it by laughing along and withdrawing at home.

qa.q: Which steps helped Akash, and why?
qa.a: Reporting the harassment to Ms Ahuja with Simran, and joining drama club, a space where he fits and is valued.

qa.q: How does Simran see what the boys are doing?
qa.a: Simran sees it as cruel and unacceptable, insisting they go to the counsellor and supporting Akash all the way.

grounding: A teen mocked for his body protects his self-respect, reports the harassment and finds a place where he fits.
